complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Set up project repository and development environment
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down the setup process into subtasks for repository initialization, folder structure creation, Node.js and Composer setup, WordPress environment configuration, .gitignore and environment variables setup, and documentation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task covers multiple setup domains (Git, Node.js, Composer, WordPress, documentation) and requires careful sequencing, but each step is well-defined and standard for modern WordPress block theme projects.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Configure build system and asset pipeline
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: List subtasks for configuring the build tool (Webpack/Vite), PostCSS, Babel, ESLint, Stylelint, asset optimization, build scripts, and source maps/watch mode.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Integrating multiple tools (build, linting, optimization) and ensuring smooth development/production workflows is complex and error-prone, requiring careful configuration and testing.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into subtasks for color palette, typography, spacing, layout, block variations, and global styles configuration in theme.json.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: theme.json is central to block themes and involves detailed configuration for design tokens and editor settings, requiring attention to both structure and design consistency[1][2].

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: List subtasks for creating each required template (index, single, archive, page, 404, search), ensuring semantic HTML and accessibility.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Each template is a discrete deliverable, but all must follow block markup, accessibility, and responsive design standards, making the task moderately complex.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into subtasks for header, footer, sidebar creation, accessibility enhancements, and responsive/mobile support.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Template parts are modular but must be robust, accessible, and reusable, requiring careful markup and testing.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into subtasks for global styles, component styles, block styles, template styles, utilities, custom properties, and responsive/print styles.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: A modular CSS architecture with PostCSS, variables, and responsive utilities is foundational and impacts maintainability and theme.json integration[1][2].

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: List subtasks for each custom block (hero, service cards, team profiles, testimonials, CTA), including registration, edit/save components, styles, and accessibility.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Custom block development involves React, block.json, editor integration, and accessibility, making it one of the most technically demanding tasks[2][4].

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into subtasks for each layout block (container, columns, spacer, divider), inspector controls, responsive behavior, and accessibility.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Layout blocks require advanced block development skills, inspector controls, and responsive logic, but are less content-heavy than core content blocks.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into subtasks for each interactive block (contact form, newsletter, social links, gallery, video), validation, accessibility, error handling, and performance.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Interactive blocks involve complex state management, validation, security, and accessibility, making this one of the most challenging tasks[2][4].

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement custom post types and taxonomies
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: List subtasks for each CPT (services, team, portfolio), taxonomy registration, meta fields, admin UI, REST API integration, and template support.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Custom post types and taxonomies require PHP, admin UI, REST API, and template integration, with moderate complexity for experienced WordPress developers.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into subtasks for each pattern (hero, services grid, about, testimonial, team, contact, FAQ), registration, and documentation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Block patterns are mostly markup and registration, but require design consistency and editor integration for usability[2][5].

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into subtasks for semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, color/contrast, forms, responsive/adaptable design, testing, and documentation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Accessibility is cross-cutting, requiring updates to markup, styles, and scripts across the theme, and thorough testing for compliance.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: List subtasks for critical CSS, JS optimization, asset optimization, caching, resource hints, image optimization, lazy loading, and performance testing.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Performance optimization spans frontend and backend, requiring deep knowledge of build tools, WordPress hooks, and browser behavior.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into subtasks for responsive images, next-gen formats, lazy loading, custom sizes, compression, and accessibility.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Media optimization involves PHP, frontend, and server-side logic, but is well-supported by WordPress filters and plugins.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into subtasks for deployment scripts, WPEngine config, environment settings, deployment documentation, testing, and rollback procedures.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Deployment configuration is procedural but must account for environment-specific nuances and documentation for reliability.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: List subtasks for input sanitization, nonce verification, file security, authentication, security headers, WordPress hardening, testing, and documentation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Security is critical and cross-cutting, requiring updates to code, configuration, and deployment, with high risk if not done thoroughly.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into subtasks for each documentation section (getting started, developer, blocks, customization, deployment, troubleshooting), markdown formatting, and review.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Comprehensive documentation is time-consuming and requires coordination with all technical areas, but is essential for maintainability and onboarding.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Expand into subtasks for JS unit tests, PHP unit tests, E2E tests, accessibility tests, performance tests, CI/CD integration, test coverage, and reporting.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: A robust testing framework spans multiple languages and tools, requiring integration and automation for quality assurance.
